items.title: VJ Edgecombe details LeBron James’ FaceTime on decision that left him ‘geekin’
items.content:
lebron james vj edgecombe 76ers lakersThe Philadelphia 76ers won the LeBron James free agent sweepstakes this summer.

VJ Edgecombe, like many basketball fans, was extremely excited to welcome the four-time NBA champion to the team. The 21-year-old had the chance to speak with James directly after the two-year, $8 million deal was announced, which he detailed during an interview at the ABCD Basketball Camp.

VJ Edgecombe was born two years after LeBron James made his NBA debut in 2003. Now, they’re teammates.  NBAE via Getty Images“I FaceTimed Bron. I was in disbelief, but I had to act cool. I had to act like I’d been there before. I’m on the phone all cool and stuff. My headphones on, I’m playing the game. Had to act all cool, but it’s really Bron. I was really geekin’ I ain’t gone lie,” Edgecombe said.

VJ Edgecombe said he was gaming when LeBron FaceTimed him pic.twitter.com/bKWMFQ2iSq

— Overtime (@overtime) August 6, 2026The ongoing free agency saga surrounding James was the headline story of the NBA summer and the 41-year-old’s decision to join the 76ers was quite the stunning denouement. 

James is set to star alongside Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey as well as the young rising star in Edgecombe.

The latter of who was born in 2005, two years after James made his NBA debut in 2003. Now, Edgecombe and James are set to be teammates, which makes the guard’s giddiness that much more authentic as he quite literally grew up watching the NBA’s all-time leading scorer. 

The 76ers face immense pressure to win a championship this upcoming season and Philadelphia’s roster is equipped to do just that. The arrival of James has made Edgecombe the fifth option for the 76ers, but he’s expected to continue developing around some of the league’s biggest stars.

At 41 years old, LeBron James was the top free agent of the summer.  Getty Images

items.title: NetsDaily Reacts: How Fans Evaluate the Brooklyn Nets 2026 Offseason
items.content:

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Zach Barron/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	With the dog days of summer officially here, we turned to Nets World to gauge the community’s perspective on the state of the franchise after the 2026 offseason. The Nets didn’t make any crazy splashes but they still had a relatively busy offseason:

The Nets drafted Mikel Brown Jr. at No. 6 overall.The Nets also traded Nic Claxton and the No. 33 pick for Julius Randle and the no. 28 overall picks (Joshua Jefferson). Brooklyn added rotational pieces like Keon Ellis and Moe Wagner.Still no word on an extension for Michael Porter Jr. While we wait, the NetsDaily community evaluated Brooklyn’s summer moves in our latest SB Nation Reacts poll. Safe to say fans think they got better!

So, what is the community saying about the Nets offseason?Most say they’re better.SoggyNetsFan: I’m giving it a much better outlook. It may not result in us doubling our win total, but not tanking, combined with having a rotation that makes more sense, will make a huge improvement. For example, Randell is an upgrade, but having a year-four Clowney coming off the bench is also a huge boost. Egor is better, and MPJ could be much improved too. Not by stats, but improved moral/effort by the fact that we aren’t trying to tank. The other sophomores who have improved over the offseason will also get opportunities to play against bench and garbage-time players rather than NBA starting-caliber ones.
Boomdog23: Just running rotations that aren’t comprised of 5rookies getting solid minutes should make us better. Not having clowney as your starting 4 is another big one.”Excitement for Mikel Brown Jr. & RandleBKtoDuval: “I’d say much better but the bar was set so low. Randle is a floor raiser. Demin is gonna be in Most Improved contention. I think the shackles will be removed from Jordi. In a limited capacity we’ve seen point guards do really well under him. Despite what SAS says, Mikel will be box office. Not to toot my horn but the past two seasons my win total futures bets have hit for Nets (and failed miserably for the Mets). So your boy BKdamas is gonna put down big money on a win total somewhere between 30-35 wins.”
NetsFan4Life: “I say adding Mikel Brown alone makes us much better.”Pessimistic or Realistic?imranetic: “the opposite is true. they are much worse and will be lucky to win 20 games. This front office ranks the lowest in the league because they don’t do anything to improve the team and have made it worse”
WhatsUp: “Irrational exuberance now that tanking is over.”

items.title: Bucks Reacts Survey Results: Jon Horst owes us an explanation
items.content:
MILWAUKEE, WI - JUNE 27: MarJon Beauchamp of the Milwaukee Bucks poses for a photo after the introductory draft press conference at Fiserv Forum on June 27, 2022 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2022 NBAE (Photo by Gary Dineen/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	This week, we’ve garnered your thoughts on trader drafter Jon. Often praised for his ability to secure heists via trade, Horst’s drafting reputation has, well… been a point of contention. 

Prior to polling, it seemed that Bucks fans were largely down on Horst as a drafter, but what seems to be consensus and what’s actually consensus are sometimes two completely different things. As a teacher, I see this all the time. On this occasion, however, the voting—and consensus—is clear: Horst sucks. 

In truth, it’s hard to ignore the reality of Horst’s draft selections. D.J. Wilson is out of the league. Jordan Nwora is too. Andre Jackson Jr. is hanging by a thread (though he may have found a lifeline), as are MarJon Beauchamp, Chris Livingston, Tyler Smith, and AJ Johnson—if they haven’t already dropped. You know it too:

G may: It was a failure in team building. There’s no reason to nuance it. He had picks. He missed worse than Rickie Weeks swinging for the fences on a curveball in the dirt in the leadoff spot.

R984: No high picks, sure. But look at where Miami picked the collection of good players we just got from them. 1 out of 6 isn’t good enough. Not nearly good enough.

Theshackman: No. And if you think about this as “overall return on draft capital” (picks traded away) it looks even worse.

While the majority of fans (51%) clearly think Horst has let the Bucks down with his selections, it’s not so cut and dry for all, with 36% of voters thinking it’s nuanced:

Knuckles: My answer then was in the middle: we need to draft better moving forward and fortify our floor, and lean into player development, but that is not where the Bucks were for a while. We have a new identity now to lean into and we should, but I also don’t want to ignore the nuance that led us to making some of these choices in the first place.

Sportsfanwisc: I went with the middle ground. The NBA as a whole gets a D grade for player development. Around the draft and polls such as this I scroll through NBA drafts as a sobering reminder out of 60 picks only 20 to 25 will play any meaningful minutes.

Kaz5: My point is only that drafting guys is really, really challenging. Even going off of the best information available at the time, no one really, truly knows what is going to happen. That doesn’t mean that you give each and every GM a pass every time, but keep in mind that nothing in the draft is certain.
